acts.title: The Gala
acts.body:
Months after the Siege of Boralus, House Duskmere has been steadily funding repairs to Tiragarde Sound. Tonight, they celebrate the work's completion with a gala at their estate.
As Champions of Azeroth, you were invited guests.
Then the toasts stopped.
Lord Alaric Duskmere has been found dead.

acts.title: The Investigation Begins
acts.body:
Captain Mira Thorne of the City Watch has arrived before the body's even cold, and takes one look at the gathered guests.
"Nobody leaves. Every single one of you is a suspect until I say otherwise. That includes our Champions of Azeroth."
The crowd begins murmuring amongst themselves as Captain Thorne turns to you.
"Which is exactly why I need your help. I don't have the manpower to watch this whole gala at once, and I trust the Champions."
"Move through the grounds, talk to people, find out who actually had reason to want Duskmere dead. Motive first. We'll worry about how it was done after."

acts.title: Investigate the Estate
acts.intro: Walk the grounds and talk to everyone: guests, suspects, staff. Most people here have nothing to hide. A few do. Pick up whatever you find and bring it back to the Evidence Table, every piece matters. Once you've got it all, Captain Thorne wants everyone up in the study.
acts.onEvidenceCompleteMessage: Captain Thorne finds you. "Good, you've found everything there is to find out here. I'm commandeering poor Alaric's office, he won't be needing it any time soon, and it gives us somewhere to go through what we've got properly. Head upstairs when you're ready to go through the evidence."

acts.title: The Evidence
acts.intro:
Everything you've found is laid out across the desk. Review it all, then work out who is a suspect.

You can go back and forth between the two as much as you need. Submit to Captain Thorne once you've decided.

dialogue.speaker: Captain Thorne
dialogue.text: Good work. Now we find out which one of them actually had the means, and the opportunity.
You go through it all one more time, right there at the desk, this time asking how, not why.

dialogue.speaker: Commodore Voss
dialogue.text: Means and opportunity, Captain? They had the run of the whole estate tonight, free to wander wherever they pleased. Plenty of quiet corners to hide something you didn't want found.
He sets a satchel on the desk and draws out a blade, dark at the edge.

dialogue.speaker: Commodore Voss
dialogue.text: Found not an hour ago. That's no rust on it, and Lord Duskmere's own manservant swears there's a mark on him to match. I'd call that convincing, wouldn't you?

dialogue.speaker: Captain Thorne
dialogue.text: I gave you a chance. Take them down to the cells.

acts.title: The Dungeons
acts.intro: You come to in separate holding cells, no way to reach each other directly. Get back together with your party, and get out of the dungeons.

dialogue.speaker: Silas "Hook" Corwin
dialogue.text:
You made it! Knew you would, but took you long enough. Hope you kept your eyes open down there, I left you a few things to find.

Come on, let's get you over to the Guild Hall and cleaned up. You reek.

acts.title: Means and Opportunity
acts.body:
Corwin brings you to the Guild Hall on the edge of the nearby village. "I knew you didn't do it," he chuckles as you walk west. "But somebody did, and I want to know who as much as you do."

"I'm resourceful; I've got some favours to call in, and a few strings left to pull. Let's use them and clear your name."

acts.title: Means and Opportunity
acts.intro:
Corwin's given you the run of his old contacts; the Training Grounds, with the Mage Tower and the Blacksmith, and the town itself, with the Tavern, the Chapel, the Glass Workshop, and the Market.

Talk to everyone. Piece together means and opportunity for each of the five names on the Suspect Board, then bring what you've found back to the board at the Guild Hall.

When the party's ready, point the finger at who you think did it.

dialogue.speaker: The Maid
dialogue.text:
She's still in her apron, like she ran the whole way. In her hands, wrapped in a cloth: a single goblet, and a folded, water-stained scrap of paper.

"I know I'm meant to be nobody in this. But I was in that kitchen. I know what was in that cellar, and I know what wasn't supposed to leave it."

dialogue.speaker: The Maid
dialogue.text:
"This was his goblet, the one nobody thought to ask about because everybody was looking at the wine bottle instead. And this," she presses the paper into your hands, "is what one of the guards actually wrote down that night, before his sergeant made him redo it."

"I know an old woman out past the east road who reads plants like other people read faces. If anyone can tell you what did this, she can."

acts.title: The Herbalist's Hut
acts.body:
Corwin leads you off the road and into the swamp, following a path only he seems to be able to see. "Old friend of mine," he says. "Owes me a favour or twelve. If anyone can tell you what killed him, she can."

The hut sits on stilts over the water, herbs drying in bundles from every rafter. A woman is already waiting at the door, arms crossed, entirely unsurprised to see you.

acts.title: What Killed Him
acts.intro: The herbalist won't just tell you what killed him. Talk to her, read whatever the maid slipped you, search her garden, and bring back whatever you think actually did it. Throw it in the cauldron and find out.

acts.title: The Finale
acts.prompt: [PLACEHOLDER: real presentation/accusation mechanic not built yet, this typed-answer box is a stopgap reusing the old Naming the Culprit code path. Design so far: you sneak back onto the estate through Corwin's tunnel and lay out everything, motive, means and opportunity, and the poison, in front of the whole household, then declare a suspect. A wrong accusation should get real pushback, that suspect arguing back with their own alibi or counter-evidence, not a vague 'try again.' Only Ashgate's correct-answer content exists so far, the other 4 finalists each need their own wrong-answer rebuttal written before this can ship.]
acts.hint: Weigh the motive, the means and opportunity, and the poison together.

acts.title: Case Closed... Or Is It?
acts.body: Lady Isobel Ashgate doesn't bother denying it once you lay it all out, motive, means, the poison itself. [PLACEHOLDER: Ashgate's actual confrontation dialogue and argument, not written yet.] The guards take her away, and as they lead her past the garden, she rounds on Old Silas Corwin, still watching from the shadows. 'Ask him,' she spits, 'what he was really doing for Alaric all these years.' Corwin doesn't answer. Thorne and Corwin see you off with a brief thanks, the case closed, at least as far as the City Watch is concerned. Take your findings back to Discord to see if it really is.
